Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Pre reading, part of Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Pre reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they work on their own in assigned tasks as they link the target

letters to their corresponding sounds in preparation for reading.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s ability to explore is enhanced as they model letter shapes for the target letters.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers in group and pair activities.

35

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: (Self- esteem) learners acquire an enhanced level of esteem as they articulate the target sounds correctly and write the corresponding letter.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner uses the pre-reading skills to learn similar concepts in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards

• Appropriate reference materials in print

• Braille reference materials
